consumer_summary.what_it_is: 4,5-diepi-Aristolochene is a sesquiterpene, a class of natural aromatic compounds often responsible for the distinct scents and defenses of plants. While not something you would typically encounter in the grocery store, it is part of the complex chemical library produced by ancient plant lineages.
consumer_summary.found_in: It has been identified in liverworts, specifically a species known as Radula lindenbergiana.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to this molecule to understand the intricate chemical machinery plants use to build complex structures. Foundational biochemical work (Oxford level 5, mechanistic research) is currently exploring the specific enzymes, like synthases, that trigger its formation. Mapping these pathways is exciting because it helps scientists understand how nature engineers these unique molecules from the ground up.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: The only available evidence consists of foundational biochemical and mechanistic research (Oxford level 5) exploring how the molecule is synthesized in plants.

evidence: Measured in 3 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.06–0.08% of total volatiles (0.012–0.016mg per chew).
